title: Nonlinear Diamagnetic Interactions in Ultrastrongly Coupled 2D Electrons
authors: Dasom Kim, Kiran M. Kulkarni, Vaibhav Sharma, Dukhyung Lee, Geon Lee, Sunghwan Kim, Jonas Grumm, Shuang Liang, Hongjing Xu, Fuyang Tay, Andrey Baydin, Motoaki Bamba, Andreas Knorr, Christopher J. Stanton, Michael J. Manfra, Minah Seo, Stephen Hughes, Junichiro Kono
abstract: The quantum Hopfield model is widely used to describe ultrastrong light--matter coupling between cavity photons and collective bosonic excitations in solids, where the diamagnetic interaction is conventionally assumed to be a constant. We experimentally demonstrate that the diamagnetic response of Landau polaritons is reduced under strong terahertz field excitation. We show that this behavior originates from field-driven redistribution of electrons into the nonparabolic regime of the conduction band of GaAs, which reduces the plasma frequency and consequently the diamagnetic interaction strength. A microscopic hot-electron model reproduces the observed nonlinear response. Motivated by this microscopic picture, we propose a nonlinear extension of the Hopfield model with a Kerr-like interaction. Our results establish a route toward nonlinear cavity quantum electrodynamics and driven ultrastrong light--matter coupling beyond the conventional linear Hopfield description, which is capable of creating uniquely quantum optical effects such as squeezed light generation.
summary: This paper reports experimental evidence and theoretical modeling showing that the diamagnetic interaction in ultrastrongly coupled electron-photon systems is nonlinear. The nonlinearity arises from the field-driven redistribution of electrons into the nonparabolic conduction band, necessitating an extension of the standard Hopfield model with Kerr-like terms.
main_problem: The study investigates the nonlinear diamagnetic response of Landau polaritons in ultrastrongly coupled systems, challenging the assumptions of the conventional linear Hopfield model.
main_result: The authors experimentally and theoretically demonstrate that intense THz driving fields cause a field-induced reduction in the diamagnetic shift by driving electrons into the nonparabolic regime of the conduction band.
method: The work combines nonlinear THz transmission spectroscopy measurements with a microscopic hot-electron model to reproduce the observed field-dependent renormalization of the plasma frequency.
model_or_system: The system involves 2D electrons (GaAs) coupled to a THz cavity, modeled using an extension of the Hopfield Hamiltonian that incorporates a Kerr-like, nonlinear interaction term derived from the nonparabolic band structure.
key_observables: Diamagnetic shift ($\Delta\omega$), polariton frequencies ($\omega_{\pm}$), and the resonance frequency ($\omega'_{	ext{cav}}$) as a function of incident THz field strength ($E_0$).
important_parameters: Ultrastrong coupling regime ($g/\omega_{	ext{cav}} \geq 0.1$), high driving fields ($E_0$ up to 2.4 kV/cm), and the electron temperature ($T_e$).
main_assumptions: The primary nonlinear effect is attributed to the thermal redistribution of electrons within the nonparabolic conduction band, and the analysis uses the semiclassical Boltzmann equation.
figures_summary: Figures show the evolution of Landau polariton frequencies with magnetic field and, critically, the redshift of the resonance frequency in THz transmission spectra as the incident THz field strength increases.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the standard linear model, presents experimental measurements showing nonlinear field dependence, develops a microscopic hot-electron model linking field strength to electron temperature, and finally proposes a nonlinear extension of the quantum Hamiltonian to describe the observed physics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the limits of standard linear cavity QED models by incorporating strong-field, non-equilibrium effects (hot-electron dynamics) into the Hamiltonian, which is highly relevant for advanced quantum optics.
